meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: immediately (with short extensions if the payroll unit is not operating)
facts.summary: Colorado: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately (with short extensions if the payroll unit is not operating).
facts.evidence_quote: (1) (a) When an interruption in the employer-employee relationship by volition of the employer occurs, the wages or compensation for labor or service earned, vested, determinable, and unpaid at the time of such discharge is due and payable immediately.
facts.source_title: Colorado Wage Act (C.R.S. 8-4-109), CDLE compilation revised August 12, 2026
facts.source_publisher: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment
facts.notes: If the accounting unit is not operating: within 6 hours of its next regular workday, or 24 hours if off site (same subsection).

facts.summary: Colorado: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due upon the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: (b) When an employee quits or resigns such employee's employment, the wages or compensation shall become due and payable upon the next regular payday.
facts.source_title: Colorado Wage Act (C.R.S. 8-4-109), CDLE compilation revised August 12, 2026
facts.source_publisher: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Colorado basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.16.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.16 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Daily - 12, Weekly - 40 Minimum wage rate and overtime provisions applicable to retail and service, commercial support service, food and beverage, and health and medical industries.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Colorado new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Colorado: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Colorado is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Colorado 2026 new (introductory) employer base UI rate, non-construction: 1.53%. With the support rate and solvency surcharge the total is 3.05%.
facts.evidence_quote: 2026 Introductory Rates Business Classification Beginning Rate Support Rate Surcharge Rate Combined Rate Non-construction 0.0153 .0017 .0135 0.0305
facts.source_title: Introductory Rates (Colorado Department of Labor and Employment)
facts.source_publisher: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment
facts.notes: Rate basis: base (beginning) rate. 2026 total with 0.17% support rate and 1.35% solvency surcharge: 3.05% (see CO.ui.total_new_employer_rate). Heavy construction base 4.28%. Matches DOL Significant Provisions (1.53%).

facts.summary: Colorado experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.56% to 7.34%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law.

facts.summary: Colorado state unemployment taxable wage base: $30,600 per employee.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance

facts.summary: Colorado 2026 total new employer UI rate (non-construction): 3.05%.
facts.source_title: Introductory Rates (Colorado Department of Labor and Employment)
facts.source_publisher: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment
facts.notes: 1.53% base + 0.17% support + 1.35% solvency surcharge. Heavy construction 6.285%. 2027: 1.70%.
